{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":139601,"idEra":21703,"activityNumber":"1000042056","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-12615","title":"CCSDS DELAY-TOLERANT NETWORKING BPSEC MODULE - EXPRO PLUS","description":"Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) is a network architecture approach that seeks to address the technical issues in heterogeneous networks that may lack continuous network connectivity. Such networks are planned networks in space.To provide a shared framework for application development in DTNs, the bundle protocol (BP) has been standardised, which defines a series of contiguous data blocks as a bundle where each bundle contains enough semantic information to allow the application to make progress where an individual block may not.Bundles are routed in a store and forward manner between participating nodes over varied network transport technologies. The BP for Consultative Committee for Space Data Systems (CCSDS) is a profile of standardized by Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) with protocol RFC 9171/9172 specifically addressing the BP's utility for data communication (including security) in space missions.CCSDS DTN is currently developing a security architecture. Its first element is the so-called Bundle Protocol Security (BPSec), standardised by IETF (RFC 9172) and is also currently in a standards development track in CCSDS. BPSec will provide a security service(confidentiality and integrity) to the DTN BP.Missions that will interface with a DTN architecture will probably require to provide security services at their DTN nodes implementations. Thus, an implementation of the DTN BPSec will be needed.Following the above, the implementation of DTN BPSec is vital in order to support interplanetary missions, deep space missions, etc. using heterogeneous networks, aiming to address lack of continuous network connectivity in such scenarios.
